notes: Each program prints '<bench> <lang> <ms> <checksum>'; ms = compute wall time measured inside the program.
Median of 5 runs. Checksums must agree across languages per benchmark (checksums_agree).

C++ compiled with -O3 -march=native -ffp-contract=off -fopenmp; the -ffp-contract=off flag disables FMA contraction so checksums are bit-identical with Go/Rust/Python (strict IEEE-754 double rounding).

nbody uses 100 Euler steps (not 200000): the step count is tuned so CPython finishes in reasonable time; the workload is otherwise identical in all languages (same N=1024, dt, softening, LCG init, two-phase update).
Threading: 2 CPU cores; parallel benchmarks use all cores where natural (OpenMP/rayon/goroutines); Python is serial.

bend2 (Bend 2.0.34 installed OK): omitted from measurements -- Bend's Base library currently provides only U32/F32 numerics (no F64/U64), so the f64 workloads cannot be ported with checksum-identical results, and its tree-based Array makes a 1e8 sieve / JSON parsing impractical.

rpc.notes: Python localhost. gRPC: grpcio server (16 worker threads) over a Unix-domain socket (TCP localhost was unusable: this VM's egress proxy env vars hijack grpc's HTTP/2 client connections). REST: stdlib ThreadingHTTPServer on 127.0.0.1:8000, POST /echo. Sequential: 2000 calls, p50/p99 per-call latency. Concurrent: 8 clients x 5s, throughput req/s. Deterministic payload bytes (random.Random(1234)).

go.notes: Go echo benchmark on 2-CPU VM, localhost TCP, no TLS. gRPC: grpc-go server on 127.0.0.1:50051 via grpc.NewServer() with DEFAULT options; client: single grpc.ClientConn (grpc.NewClient + insecure credentials), reused across all calls. REST: net/http server on 127.0.0.1:8080 (default http.Server, no timeouts), POST /echo reads full body, writes it back with Content-Length; client: single http.Client with keep-alives (MaxIdleConnsPerHost=16), reused. Payload: deterministic bytes from math/rand seed 1234, verified byte-identical on every response (abort on mismatch). seq N: 2000 calls for 1KB/64KB, 500 for 1MB, 100 for 16MB. conc: 8 goroutine clients x 5s. Versions: go1.25.1, google.golang.org/grpc v1.84.0, google.golang.org/protobuf v1.36.12, protoc 31.1, protoc-gen-go v1.36.12, protoc-gen-go-grpc 1.6.2. CAVEAT: grpc-go defaults cap messages at 4MB, so 16MB echo FAILED with defaults (ResourceExhausted: received message larger than max 16777221 vs 4194304). The grpc 16MB figures are a bonus run on 127.0.0.1:50052 with ONLY MaxRecvMsgSize/MaxSendMsgSize raised to 32MB on both server and client call options; all other settings identical. REST handled 16MB with defaults.

rust.notes: Rust echo benchmark on 2-CPU VM, localhost TCP, no TLS. gRPC: tonic server on 127.0.0.1:50051 (tonic::transport::Server defaults; echo handler clones the bytes payload). REST: axum 0.8 server on 127.0.0.1:8080 (default axum::serve; POST /echo reads the full body and writes it back; DefaultBodyLimit::disable() was set because axum rejects bodies >2MB by default). Clients reuse one tonic Channel / one reqwest Client (keep-alive) across all calls. Payload: deterministic bytes from rand StdRng::seed_from_u64(1234), freshly seeded per payload size; EVERY response byte-compared against the request payload, abort on mismatch (zero mismatches in all accepted runs). seq N: 2000 calls for 1KB/64KB, 500 for 1MB, 100 for 16MB. conc: 8 tasks x 5s, throughput req/s. tonic defaults cap messages at 4MB: the 16MB gRPC run failed with defaults (OutOfRange: decoded message length too large: found 16777221 bytes, the limit is: 4194304 bytes); the reported 16MB gRPC numbers are a bonus run with MAX_MSG_MB=32 raising max_decoding/max_encoding_message_size to 32MB on both server and client. One contaminated run was discarded: stale Go benchmark servers left from an earlier session were still bound to the ports during the first Rust attempt; they were killed, ports verified free, and the full matrix re-run clean. One REST 16MB attempt with axum's default 2MB body limit was rejected (413) and re-run with the limit disabled. Versions: rustc 1.98.1, tonic 0.12.3, prost 0.13.5, tonic-build 0.12.3, axum 0.8.9, reqwest 0.12.28, tokio 1.53.1, rand 0.10.3, protoc 31.1 (real codegen via build.rs).

structured.notes: Rust structured-payload echo benchmark on 2-CPU VM, localhost TCP, no TLS. Catalog proto: Item{id,name,description,price,quantity,tags[3],in_stock,created_at,category,rating} x N, service CatalogService.Echo. Data: deterministic from StdRng seed 1234; name=product-%06d, description=20 lorem words (~120 chars), price=2-decimal 0-1000, quantity 0-999, 3 tags tag-00..49, in_stock p=0.8, created_at=1700000000+i, category cycles 8 values, rating 1.0-5.0. SAME generated structs used for both protocols (tonic-build type_attribute adds serde Serialize/Deserialize to the prost types), so identical logical data on the wire; every response compared as full struct, abort on mismatch (zero mismatches). gRPC: tonic server 127.0.0.1:50051 defaults; REST: axum 127.0.0.1:8080 POST /echo Json<Catalog>, defaults. No config changes from defaults: largest protobuf payload 1,167,388 bytes < tonic 4MB cap; largest JSON 1,698,601 bytes < axum 2MB body limit. Clients reuse one tonic Channel / one reqwest Client (keep-alive). seq N: 2000 (10 items), 200 (500), 50 (5000). conc: 8 tasks x 5 s. wire_bytes = serialized message body only (protobuf encode_to_vec / serde_json string length); HTTP/2 frames+headers and HTTP/1.1 headers excluded. Crate versions: tonic 0.12.3, prost 0.13.5, tonic-build 0.12.3, axum 0.8.9, reqwest 0.12.28, tokio 1.53.1, rand 0.9.5, serde 1.0.229, serde_json 1.0.151; rustc 1.98.1; protoc 31.1 (real codegen via build.rs). Caveat: conc mode shares one tonic Channel (single multiplexed h2 connection) vs reqwest connection pool; 10-item p99s show scheduling noise typical of sub-ms localhost measurements on 2 CPUs.
